Yes, that completes it. Typing `"and"` in quotes treated it as the plain word — the CSS grid and empty-states bookmarks stayed because their descriptions actually contain the standalone word "and," while the JavaScript tutorial stayed hidden since "advanced" just happens to have those letters buried inside it, not the real word. So quoting a command word makes it search for that word literally instead of acting as an operator, and it matches whole words rather than fragments. That's exactly what I intended.

The whole search side now feels complete to me — plain text across titles, descriptions, notes, and addresses; ignoring capitals; label search with `#`; and/or/not with grouping; exact phrases; and quoting the command words. Nicely done. What would you like to look at next?
